definition: Accentuate means to stress or highlight something — to make a real feature more noticeable or prominent.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word accentuate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know accentuate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The gallery hung one small lamp above each canvas, angled to accentuate the brushwork rather than flood it with light.
Note is milder than accentuate: to note a detail is simply to mention it once and move on, while accentuating it shapes the whole presentation so the detail stands out.
Exaggerate goes further than accentuate — accentuating strengthens what is truly there, but exaggerating inflates it past the truth into something the facts no longer support.

To highlight is to pick something out for attention — a marker stripe, a pointed mention. Highlighting aims eyes at a feature from outside; accentuating works on the feature itself, strengthening it until it speaks up on its own.

To underscore is to insist on a point's importance, the spoken equivalent of underlining. Underscore belongs to arguments and warnings; accentuate belongs to features and contrasts — you underscore a danger, you accentuate a silhouette.

Accentuate means to stress or highlight something — to make a real feature more noticeable or prominent.
A good stage-makeup artist doesn't redraw an actor's face; she accentuates what the back row would otherwise miss — a brow line here, a shadow there — until the same features carry to the last seat.
Accentuate names emphasis that stays honest: the artist strengthens features the actor already has, and stops where the truth stops.
Redrawing the face would be invention; accentuating only turns up what is really there.
Accentuate stays inside the truth: it strengthens a feature that is really there, and stops where the facts stop — push past them and you are exaggerating instead.
It also works on the thing itself; to aim attention from outside — a mention, a marker — is to highlight.
A belt accentuates a waist; a footnote highlights a source.
